Strongly data-driven via **ScriptableObjects** in `Assets/_Scripts/Data/`:
- `CardDataSO` (`[CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "Data/CardDataSO")]`): Description, Mana, Image, **`[SerializeReference, SR] Effect ManualTargetEffect`** (polymorphic serialization via `SerializeReferenceEditor`), `List<AutoTargetEffect> OtherEffects`, CardType, CardRarityType, base/upgrade stats (damage/block/magic/mana), `upgradeName`, `CanBeUpgradeInfinitely`.

- `CardPoolDataSO`, `EnemyPoolDataSO`, `PerkPoolDataSO` (pools), `PerkDataSO`, `HeroDataSO` (hero stats + starting `Deck`).

### 4. Key Classes & Interfaces
- `GameAction` (abstract): chainable command with Pre/Perform/Post reaction lists.
- Concrete GameActions (GameActions/): `AddBuffGA`, `AddDefenceGA`, `AddStatusEffectGA`, `AttackHeroGA`, `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, `DealDamageGA` (holds `List<DamageInfo>`), `DiscardAllCardsGA`, `DrawCardsGA`, `EnemyTurnGA`, `EnterRoomGA`, `KillEnemyGA`, `PerformEffectGA`, `PlayCardGA`, `RefillManaGA`, `RegainHPGA`, `SpendManaGA`, `UpdateAwardByRoomTypeGA`.

- `DamageInfo` (Info/): attacker, target, baseDamage, currentDamage, sourceCard — used by buff hooks to modify damage.

1. `MatchSetupSystem.Start()` → `HeroSystem.Setup(heroDataSO)` builds hero + starting deck; starting `Perk`s added via `PerkSystem.AddPerk`; `Layer=1`, `CurrentRoomType=Monster`.
2. `MapController.Start()` → `GenerateAndDrawMap()` → `MapGenerator.GenerateMap()`.
3. Player clicks a `MapNodeView` → `EnterRoomGA` → `EnterRoomPerformer`: `Layer++`, `EnemySystem.Setup(enemyDataSO)` spawns enemies, `CardSystem.SetUpClonedCard(HeroSystem.Instance.Deck)`, then reactions `RefillManaGA` + `DrawCardsGA(5)` → **player turn starts** (5-card hand).
4. Player plays cards (`PlayCardGA`): spend mana → (manual effect on click-target) → auto-targeted effects via `PerformEffectGA` → each Effect returns its own GameAction (damage/block/buff/draw) queued as reactions. Damage goes through `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage` (buff modification) and `CombatantView.Damage` (armor→HP); enemy death → `KillEnemyGA`.
5. Player ends turn (`EndTurnButtonUI`) → `EnemyTurnGA`: PRE reactions (discard hand, show "敌人回合"), performer (each enemy queues `AttackHeroGA` → `DealDamageGA`), POST reactions (buff turn-end via `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, draw 5, show "玩家回合"). ### 6. Card System
Cards = `Card` model wrapping `CardDataSO`. CardView displays title/description/mana/type with **dynamic text replacement**: `{damage}` / `{block}` / `{magic}` placeholders replaced by live preview values (buffs applied via `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage`), refreshed whenever buffs change. - UI communicates with logic **only through the action system and events** (no direct mutation): e.g., `OnHealthChange`/`OnDefenceChange` events update bars; `CombatFeedbackSystem` renders floating damage text/buff icons; `Interactions` gates input during action execution. Chinese localization is baked into strings (e.g., `GetChinceseTypeText`).

### Gaps / Notes
- The environment deduplicated re-reads for `ManaSystem`, `AllDataSystem`, `PerkSystem`, `RestSystem`, `MerchantSystem`, `StatusEffectSystem`, `DefenceSysytem`, `HealthRegenerationSystem`, `HeroView`, `HandView`, `EnemyBoardView`, `MapUIManager`, `MapNodeView`, and several GameAction files, so those were captured earlier in context but their full bodies are not reproduced here; `MapGenerator` and `CardView` were only read partially (first ~100/120 lines). # Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, world, and audio generation capabilities via MCP.

## ⚡ Routing Priority — READ FIRST

This MCP server may coexist with the TJGenerators Unity Editor extension (custom tools via execute_custom_tool). When both are available, follow this priority:

1. **Particle/VFX effects → search_effect_lib FIRST** — before ANY generation tool (MCP or extension). The 1300+ toon-style effect library has instant downloads, zero generation wait, and is performant in Unity. Only fall back to generation if search_effect_lib finds no match after trying different keywords.

2. **Stock 3D prefabs / scene props → search_asset_lib FIRST** (or the Unity extension's search_assets when it is installed). Instant download from the Codely asset library, billed on first download. Only fall back to generate_3d_model if search finds no match.

3. **All other generation → prefer Unity extension custom tools** — the extension has Unity-scene awareness, asset tracking, and integrated import. Use MCP tools below ONLY as fallback when the extension is not installed or its tool is unavailable.

4. **MCP-exclusive tools → always use MCP** (no extension equivalent exists).

### MCP-exclusive tools (always use — no extension equivalent)

- **search_effect_lib**: Search 1300+ ready-made toon-style particle effects (explosion, fire, magic, sword hit, muzzle flash, blood, heal, weather, etc.). Instant download, no generation wait. HIGHEST PRIORITY for any particle/VFX request — try before generate_effect_video, generate_image, generate_video, or the extension's effect tools.
- **generate_music**: background music generation
- **generate_sprite_atlas**: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns immediately, no polling)
- **generate_image_layers**: 大模型图片分层 — decompose one image into a set of independent RGBA layers (前景/背景/物件分层编辑)
- **file_upload**: upload local files to CDN (see workflow below)
- **check_task**: generic async task polling for MCP-originated tasks only (extension has its own query_*_status tools)

### Redundant with extension (defer to extension; MCP is fallback only)

If the extension is installed, use the extension's equivalent tool instead of these MCP tools:
- search_asset_lib / download_asset_lib → extension: search_assets / download_asset (same generator-backend billing; extension also imports into the Unity project)
- generate_3d_model → extension: generate_3d_model_by_rodin
- generate_image → extension: generate_image
- generate_video → extension: generate_video
- generate_effect_video → extension: generate_effect_video
- generate_game_ui_kit → extension: generate_game_ui_kit (+ slice_image)
- generate_skybox → extension: generate_skybox
- generate_material → extension: generate_material
- generate_sound_effect → extension: generate_sound_effect
- generate_tts → extension: generate_tts
- upscale_image → extension: upscale_image
- voice_clone → extension: voice_clone
- generate_sprite_animation → extension: generate_sprite_sequence / generate_2d_sprite_sequence_auto
- unirig_rig → extension: generate_rigged_model
- generate_motion → extension: generate_model_motion

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_image_layers / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Fallback Tool Details (use only when extension is NOT available)

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (rodin Gen-2.5 Extreme-Low default, rodin Gen-2.5 Extreme-High for high-quality/高精度, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested; provider=hy_image_v3 / \"hy-image-v3\" / \"用混元生图\" uses Tencent TokenHub 混元图像3.0). With provider=seedream_pro + layer_decomposition=true: decomposes ONE input image into a base image + up to 16 transparent PNG layers with metadata (see also generate_image_layers)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_image_layers: decompose one image into a set of independent RGBA layers (大模型图片分层). Two providers: qwen (default, 1-8 layers, prompt required) and seedream_pro (Seedream 5.0 Pro layer decomposition: 1 base image + up to 16 transparent PNG layers with z_index/name/description/bounding_box metadata, prompt optional, auto layer count).
- generate_sound_effect / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Fallback Sprite Animation & UI (use only when extension is NOT available)

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot (Seedream 5.0 Pro by default); Step 2 decomposes it into transparent UI-element PNG layers with per-layer metadata (provider=frontier keeps the legacy magenta cutout-sheet path)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Fallback Rigging & Motion (use only when extension is NOT available)

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async), plus ready-made poll commands in their structured output: poll_command for bash/Git Bash (macOS, Linux) and poll_command_powershell for Windows PowerShell, both curl loops against poll_url with the per-task poll_interval_seconds.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
IMPORTANT: For each async task, launch ONE background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to wait for it — spawn one subagent per task to run tasks concurrently.
The subagent must NOT call check_task in a loop: it should run the poll command matching its shell (poll_command in bash, poll_command_powershell in Windows PowerShell — never run the bash one in PowerShell), wait for it to finish, then call check_task ONCE with the task_id to fetch the full result (output URLs, guides) and report a concise summary back.
For chained workflows (e.g. generate_game_ui_kit step 1 → step 2), the same subagent can start the next step after check_task returns the previous step's output.

## Slay the Spire Reprint — Architecture Analysis (Assets/_Scripts)

### 1. Architecture Overview
The project uses a **hybrid architecture** centered on a custom **Command / Action-Queue pattern** combined with **Singleton "System" services** and **Model–View separation**. Key characteristics:

- **ActionSystem (Command pattern + Observer)**: `General/ActionSystem.cs` is a global singleton orchestrator. Every game action is a `GameAction` object (abstract base in `GameActions/GameAction.cs`) with three reaction lists: `PreReactions`, `PerformReactions`, `PostReactions` — enabling **chain reactions** (a played card's effects spawn nested GameActions). The system exposes:
  - `Perform(GameAction)` → runs a coroutine `Flow()` that (1) invokes PRE subscribers, (2) runs performer coroutine, (3) runs POST subscribers, while recursively executing reactions.
  - `AttachPerformer<T>(Func<T,IEnumerator>)` — each system registers the *executor* for a GameAction type (a **strategy/command handler** registry).
  - `SubscribeReaction<T>(Action<T>, ReactionTiming.PRE/POST)` — event-driven reactions to specific action types (observer pattern).
  - Performers are attached in `OnEnable()` / detached in `OnDisable()` of each system MonoBehaviour.
- **Service locator / Singleton pattern**: Nearly every system is a static singleton (`CardSystem.Instance`, `EnemySystem.Instance`, `HeroSystem.Instance`, `DamageSystem.Instance`, `BuffSystem.Instance`, `AwardSystem.Instance`, `MatchSetupSystem.Instance`, `Interactions.Instance`, `ActionSystem.Instance`, `AllDataSystem.Instance`, `MapController.Instance`...). Awake enforces single instance (destroys duplicates).
- **Model–View separation**: Runtime data classes (`Card`, `Effect`, `Perk`, `Award`, `CardDataSO`, `EnemyDataSO`) are separate from visual MonoBehaviour views (`CardView`, `HeroView`, `EnemyView`, `CombatantView`, `HandView`, views created via `Creators/CardViewCreator`, `Creators/EnemyViewCreator` — simple factory classes).
- **Data-driven design**: `ScriptableObject` data assets + `[SerializeReference]` for polymorphic effects.
- Comments are in Chinese (zh-CN), indicating a Chinese-language dev team.

### 2. Core Systems (Systems/ subdirectory)
- **CardSystem** (singleton): Manages draw/discard/hand piles (`List<Card>`), `SetUp(deckData)`, `SetUpClonedCard`, drawing (`DrawCardsPerformer` with reshuffle when deck empty), discarding all (`DiscardAllCardsGA`), and `PlayCardPerformer` — the heart of card play: removes card from hand, plays discard animation, adds `SpendManaGA`, then for the manual-target effect and each auto-target effect adds `PerformEffectGA` reactions. It also implements `GenerateCard()` with rarity roll (Common 65% / Uncommon 25% / Rare 10%) and Chinese type text.
- **EnemySystem** (singleton): `Setup(List<EnemyDataSO>)` spawns enemy views via `EnemyBoardView.AddEnemy`; `EnemyTurnPerformer` triggers each enemy's attack via `AttackHeroGA`; `AttackHeroPerformer` does a lunge animation then adds `DealDamageGA`; `KillEnemyPerformer` removes the view and, when the board is empty, calls `AwardSystem.AwardShow()` + discard-all. Registers PRE/POST reactions to show "敌人回合"/"玩家回合" turn text.
- **DamageSystem**: `DealDamagePerformer` iterates `DamageInfo` list, shows damage text/VFX via `CombatFeedbackSystem`, calls `target.Damage(damage)`, and queues `KillEnemyGA` when an enemy's HP reaches 0 (player death is a stub). Static `CalculateDamage(DamageInfo)` runs attacker's `ModifyDamageGive` buffs then target's `ModifyDamageTaken` buffs; result clamped ≥ 0.
- **EffectSystem**: `PerformEffectPerformer(PerformEffectGA)` calls the polymorphic `Effect.GetGameAction(targets, caster, sourceCard)` and adds the returned GameAction as a reaction — bridging Effects → GameActions. Always passes `HeroSystem.Instance.HeroView` as default caster.
- **BuffSystem**: `AddBuffGAPerformer` applies buffs to targets and refreshes card preview text when the hero is affected; `AtTurnEndBuffGAPerform` iterates enemy buffs then hero buffs calling `AtTurnEnd()`. Reacts POST to `EnemyTurnGA`.
- **HeroSystem**: Holds `HeroView`, the player's `Deck` (List<Card>), `AddCard` (raises `AddCardEvent`), and deck UI toggle.
- **AwardSystem**: Generates rewards by room type (`UpdateAwardsByRoomType`): Monster→Coin+Card, Elite→Coin+Card+Perk, Treasure→Coin+Perk; shows `AwardUI` / `CardAwarPanelUI`; manages award views to destroy.
- **MatchSetupSystem**: Global match state (`HeroDataSO`, enemy list, perks, `Coin`, `Layer`, `CurrentRoomType`). `Start()` sets up hero, adds starting perks. `EnterRoomPerformer(EnterRoomGA)` increments layer, sets up enemies, clones hero deck into draw pile, adds `RefillManaGA` + `DrawCardsGA(5)` reactions.
- **Other systems**: `ManaSystem` (mana/energy; `RefillManaGA`/`SpendManaGA`), `PerkSystem` (relics), `StatusEffectSystem`, `DefenceSysytem` (sic), `HealthRegenerationSystem`, `RestSystem` (campfire heal/upgrade), `TestSystem`, `CardViewHoverSystem`, `CombatFeedbackSystem` (VFX/text/turn banner), `manualTargetSystem` (click-target selection), `ReactionTiming` (enum PRE/POST), `Interactions` (input gating — blocks interaction while `ActionSystem.IsPerforming`; tracks `PlayerIsDragging`).
- **Buff/**: `BuffBase` (abstract: `Amount`, `owner`, `DeepClone`, hooks `OnApply`, `OnRemove`, `AtTurnStart`, `AtTurnEnd` (decrements and removes at 0), `OnPlayCard`, `ModifyDamageTaken`, `ModifyDamageGive`, `GetDescription`), concrete `StrengthBuff`, `VulnerableBuff` (+ typo'd filename `VulnerableBuff .cs`), plus `BuffsUI`, `BuffUI`.
- **Effects/**: `DealDamageEffect`, `AddDefenceEffect`, `AddBuffEffect`, `AddStatusEffectEffect`, `DrawCardEffect` — all derive from `Models/Effect.cs` (abstract, `GetGameAction(...)`).
- **TatgetModes/ (sic)**: `AllEnemiesTM`, `HeroTM`, `NoTM`, `RandomEnemyTM` implement target selection for `AutoTargetEffect`.
- **PerkContions/ (sic)**: `OnEnemyAttackCondition` — conditional perk triggers.
- **Merchant/**: `MerchantSystem`, `PlayerGoldSystem`, `MerchantItemData`, `MerchantItemUI`, `CardItemUI`, `CardItemNoGoldView`, `PerkItemUI`, `ItemUI`, `MerchantItemType`.
- **Models/Award/**: `Award` base + `CoinAward`, `CardAward`, `PerkAward`.

### 3. Data-Driven Design
Strongly data-driven via **ScriptableObjects** in `Assets/_Scripts/Data/`:
- `CardDataSO` (`[CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "Data/CardDataSO")]`): Description, Mana, Image, **`[SerializeReference, SR] Effect ManualTargetEffect`** (polymorphic serialization via `SerializeReferenceEditor`), `List<AutoTargetEffect> OtherEffects`, CardType, CardRarityType, base/upgrade stats (damage/block/magic/mana), `upgradeName`, `CanBeUpgradeInfinitely`.
- `EnemyDataSO`: id, Image, Health, AttckPower.
- `EncounterDataSO`: holds `List<EnemyDataSO> EnemyDataSos` (per-node encounter).
- `CardPoolDataSO`, `EnemyPoolDataSO`, `PerkPoolDataSO` (pools), `PerkDataSO`, `HeroDataSO` (hero stats + starting `Deck`).
- `AllDataSystem` (Systems/): central runtime registry singleton exposing `AllCardsDataSO`, `IroncladCardPool` (CardPoolDataSO), `PerkPoolDataSO.PerkPool`, etc. — referenced by CardSystem and AwardSystem.
- **Models wrap data**: `Card` wraps a `CardDataSO` (runtime stats copied into `BaseDamage/BaseBlock/BaseMagic/Mana`, mutable `Upgrade()` logic, `Clone()`); `Perk` wraps `PerkDataSO`. Effects are `[Serializable]` abstract classes serialized *inside* the SOs using SerializeReference — a notable use of Unity's polymorphic serialization (SRE asset).
- Data assets live in `Assets/Data` (referenced by the SO scripts); I confirmed the script structure but did not enumerate every .asset file.

### 4. Key Classes & Interfaces
- `GameAction` (abstract): chainable command with Pre/Perform/Post reaction lists.
- Concrete GameActions (GameActions/): `AddBuffGA`, `AddDefenceGA`, `AddStatusEffectGA`, `AttackHeroGA`, `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, `DealDamageGA` (holds `List<DamageInfo>`), `DiscardAllCardsGA`, `DrawCardsGA`, `EnemyTurnGA`, `EnterRoomGA`, `KillEnemyGA`, `PerformEffectGA`, `PlayCardGA`, `RefillManaGA`, `RegainHPGA`, `SpendManaGA`, `UpdateAwardByRoomTypeGA`.
- `Effect` (abstract) → effect implementations; `AutoTargetEffect` (wraps `Effect` + `TargetMode`); `TargetMode` (abstract) → TargetMode implementations.
- `CombatantView` (abstract-ish MonoBehaviour): shared hero/enemy base — Health/MaxHealth, `CurrentDefence`, `AddDefence`, `Damage` (armor absorbs first, then HP, triggers hit-stop + CameraShake + shake anim), dictionaries for buffs (List) & status effects, `AddBuff` (stacks by `BuffId` with `DeepClone`), events `OnHealthChange` / `OnDefenceChange`.
- `HeroView` / `EnemyView` (both extend `CombatantView`); `EnemyView` has `AttckPower` and `Setup(EnemyDataSO)`.
- `DamageInfo` (Info/): attacker, target, baseDamage, currentDamage, sourceCard — used by buff hooks to modify damage.
- Interfaces: `IHaveCaster` (Interfaces/), `IBuff`-style hooks live as virtual methods on `BuffBase` (no separate IBuff interface found).
- Enums (Enums/): `AwardType`, `CardRarityType` (Common/Uncommon/Rare), `CardType` (Attack/Skill/Power), `StatusEffectType`; `RoomType` is declared in `Map/MapNode.cs`.
- `ReactionTiming` enum (PRE/POST) in Systems/.

### 5. Game Flow
1. `MatchSetupSystem.Start()` → `HeroSystem.Setup(heroDataSO)` builds hero + starting deck; starting `Perk`s added via `PerkSystem.AddPerk`; `Layer=1`, `CurrentRoomType=Monster`.
2. `MapController.Start()` → `GenerateAndDrawMap()` → `MapGenerator.GenerateMap()`.
3. Player clicks a `MapNodeView` → `EnterRoomGA` → `EnterRoomPerformer`: `Layer++`, `EnemySystem.Setup(enemyDataSO)` spawns enemies, `CardSystem.SetUpClonedCard(HeroSystem.Instance.Deck)`, then reactions `RefillManaGA` + `DrawCardsGA(5)` → **player turn starts** (5-card hand).
4. Player plays cards (`PlayCardGA`): spend mana → (manual effect on click-target) → auto-targeted effects via `PerformEffectGA` → each Effect returns its own GameAction (damage/block/buff/draw) queued as reactions. Damage goes through `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage` (buff modification) and `CombatantView.Damage` (armor→HP); enemy death → `KillEnemyGA`.
5. Player ends turn (`EndTurnButtonUI`) → `EnemyTurnGA`: PRE reactions (discard hand, show "敌人回合"), performer (each enemy queues `AttackHeroGA` → `DealDamageGA`), POST reactions (buff turn-end via `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, draw 5, show "玩家回合"). (`CardSystem` and `EnemySystem` both subscribe to `EnemyTurnGA` PRE/POST.)
6. Victory: when all enemies die, `AwardSystem.AwardShow()`; rewards generated per `UpdateAwardsByRoomType` (coins/cards/perks); player returns to map.
7. Rest/Merchant/Treasure rooms handled by `RestSystem`, `MerchantSystem`, AwardSystem.
Note: `HeroSystem`/`HeroView` could not be fully re-read (tool dedup), but their key APIs were captured.

### 6. Card System
Cards = `Card` model wrapping `CardDataSO`. CardView displays title/description/mana/type with **dynamic text replacement**: `{damage}` / `{block}` / `{magic}` placeholders replaced by live preview values (buffs applied via `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage`), refreshed whenever buffs change. Card play is fully action-driven (see 5). - **Models wrap data**: `Card` wraps a `CardDataSO` (runtime stats copied into `BaseDamage/BaseBlock/BaseMagic/Mana`, mutable `Upgrade()` logic, `Clone()`); `Perk` wraps `PerkDataSO`. Effects are `[Serializable]` abstract classes serialized *inside* the SOs using SerializeReference — a notable use of Unity's polymorphic serialization (SRE asset).
- Data assets live in `Assets/Data` (referenced by the SO scripts); I confirmed the script structure but did not enumerate every .asset file.

### 4. Key Classes & Interfaces
- `GameAction` (abstract): chainable command with Pre/Perform/Post reaction lists.
- Concrete GameActions (GameActions/): `AddBuffGA`, `AddDefenceGA`, `AddStatusEffectGA`, `AttackHeroGA`, `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, `DealDamageGA` (holds `List<DamageInfo>`), `DiscardAllCardsGA`, `DrawCardsGA`, `EnemyTurnGA`, `EnterRoomGA`, `KillEnemyGA`, `PerformEffectGA`, `PlayCardGA`, `RefillManaGA`, `RegainHPGA`, `SpendManaGA`, `UpdateAwardByRoomTypeGA`.
- `Effect` (abstract) → effect implementations; `AutoTargetEffect` (wraps `Effect` + `TargetMode`); `TargetMode` (abstract) → TargetMode implementations.
- `CombatantView` (abstract-ish MonoBehaviour): shared hero/enemy base — Health/MaxHealth, `CurrentDefence`, `AddDefence`, `Damage` (armor absorbs first, then HP, triggers hit-stop + CameraShake + shake anim), dictionaries for buffs (List) & status effects, `AddBuff` (stacks by `BuffId` with `DeepClone`), events `OnHealthChange` / `OnDefenceChange`.
- `HeroView` / `EnemyView` (both extend `CombatantView`); `EnemyView` has `AttckPower` and `Setup(EnemyDataSO)`.
- `DamageInfo` (Info/): attacker, target, baseDamage, currentDamage, sourceCard — used by buff hooks to modify damage.
- Interfaces: `IHaveCaster` (Interfaces/), `IBuff`-style hooks live as virtual methods on `BuffBase` (no separate IBuff interface found).
- Enums (Enums/): `AwardType`, `CardRarityType` (Common/Uncommon/Rare), `CardType` (Attack/Skill/Power), `StatusEffectType`; `RoomType` is declared in `Map/MapNode.cs`.

1. `MatchSetupSystem.Start()` → `HeroSystem.Setup(heroDataSO)` builds hero + starting deck; starting `Perk`s added via `PerkSystem.AddPerk`; `Layer=1`, `CurrentRoomType=Monster`.
2. `MapController.Start()` → `GenerateAndDrawMap()` → `MapGenerator.GenerateMap()`.
3. Player clicks a `MapNodeView` → `EnterRoomGA` → `EnterRoomPerformer`: `Layer++`, `EnemySystem.Setup(enemyDataSO)` spawns enemies, `CardSystem.SetUpClonedCard(HeroSystem.Instance.Deck)`, then reactions `RefillManaGA` + `DrawCardsGA(5)` → **player turn starts** (5-card hand).
4. Player plays cards (`PlayCardGA`): spend mana → (manual effect on click-target) → auto-targeted effects via `PerformEffectGA` → each Effect returns its own GameAction (damage/block/buff/draw) queued as reactions. Damage goes through `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage` (buff modification) and `CombatantView.Damage` (armor→HP); enemy death → `KillEnemyGA`.
5. Player ends turn (`EndTurnButtonUI`) → `EnemyTurnGA`: PRE reactions (discard hand, show "敌人回合"), performer (each enemy queues `AttackHeroGA` → `DealDamageGA`), POST reactions (buff turn-end via `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, draw 5, show "玩家回合"). (`CardSystem` and `EnemySystem` both subscribe to `EnemyTurnGA` PRE/POST.)
6. Victory: when all enemies die, `AwardSystem.AwardShow()`; rewards generated per `UpdateAwardsByRoomType` (coins/cards/perks); player returns to map.
7. Rest/Merchant/Treasure rooms handled by `RestSystem`, `MerchantSystem`, AwardSystem.
Note: `HeroSystem`/`HeroView` could not be fully re-read (tool dedup), but their key APIs were captured.

### 6. Card System
Cards = `Card` model wrapping `CardDataSO`. CardView displays title/description/mana/type with **dynamic text replacement**: `{damage}` / `{block}` / `{magic}` placeholders replaced by live preview values (buffs applied via `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage`), refreshed whenever buffs change. ### 7. Enemy/AI System
Enemies are data-driven (`EnemyDataSO`: id/Image/Health/AttckPower) instantiated as `EnemyView` (extends `CombatantView`) in an `EnemyBoardView`. AI is simple: at `EnemyTurnGA`, each enemy queues `AttackHeroGA` (lunge animation + `DealDamageGA` vs `HeroSystem.Instance.HeroView`). No per-enemy behavior scripts (no intent/relic AI) in the read files — behavior is uniform attack. Enemy death → `KillEnemyPerformer` (removes view; awards when board empty). Enemies can hold buffs and status effects (stacks: e.g., strength modifies outgoing damage via `ModifyDamageGive`).

### 8. Map System
- `MapNode` (model, `[Serializable]`): X/Y grid position, `RoomType` (Unknown/Monster/Elite/Rest/Merchant/Treasure/Mystery/Boss), optional `EncounterDataSO`, `NextNodes` adjacency list, `HasParents` connectivity flag.
- `MapGenerator` (805-line procedural generator): creates `MapNode[mapWidth,mapHeight]` grid (7×15), generates `numPaths`(6) random walks from bottom to top using path-inertia/momentum + anti-crossing + scoring toward a boss Y row; `CleanupOrphans()` removes disconnected nodes; assigns room types per node (types assigned during generation).
- `MapController`: singleton; scripted `GenerateAndDrawMap()` sizing a ScrollRect content, toggle via M/Tab; exposes generation + UI drawing.
- `MapUIManager.DrawMap(nodes, width, height)`: renders map node views; `MapNodeView` presumably hooks node clicks → room entry (not read in full).

### 9. UI System
UI is a dedicated layer under `UI/` plus `Views/` for gameplay entities:
- Views (`Views/`): `CardView` (drag/hover, description substitution, preview damage), `HandView` (fan layout, `cards` list, `AddCard`/`RemoveCard`), `HeroView`, `EnemyView`, `EnemyBoardView`, `CombatantView`, `AwardView`, `ArrowView` (targeting arrow), `CardViewCreator`/`EnemyViewCreator` factories.
- UI widgets (`UI/`): `HPBarUI`, `DefenceBarUI`, `ManaUI`, `TurnPanelUI`, `EndTurnButtonUI`, `HeroCurrentDeckUI`, `AwardUI`, `CardAwarPanelUI`, `PerksUI`/`PerkUI`, `StatusEffectsUI`/`StatusEffectUI`, `RestUI`, `UpgradingCardUI`, `ButtonGlow`, `FadePanelSystem`, `FingerSelectUI`, `CameraIdle`, `MainMenu`/`MenuButton`/`MenuTitle`.
- UI communicates with logic **only through the action system and events** (no direct mutation): e.g., `OnHealthChange`/`OnDefenceChange` events update bars; `CombatFeedbackSystem` renders floating damage text/buff icons; `Interactions` gates input during action execution. Chinese localization is baked into strings (e.g., `GetChinceseTypeText`).

### Gaps / Notes
- The environment deduplicated re-reads for `ManaSystem`, `AllDataSystem`, `PerkSystem`, `RestSystem`, `MerchantSystem`, `StatusEffectSystem`, `DefenceSysytem`, `HealthRegenerationSystem`, `HeroView`, `HandView`, `EnemyBoardView`, `MapUIManager`, `MapNodeView`, and several GameAction files, so those were captured earlier in context but their full bodies are not reproduced here; `MapGenerator` and `CardView` were only read partially (first ~100/120 lines). Deeper dives into those files (esp. `MapGenerator` scoring, `HandView` layout, `ManualTargetSystem` targeting flow, `PerkSystem` conditional logic) would complete the picture.

Next steps:
If deeper detail is required, read the remaining unread files directly: Systems/ManaSystem.cs, Systems/PerkSystem.cs, Systems/RestSystem.cs, Systems/StatusEffectSystem.cs, Systems/DefenceSysytem.cs, Systems/manualTargetSystem.cs, Merchant/MerchantSystem.cs, Merchant/PlayerGoldSystem.cs, Views/HandView.cs, Views/HeroView.cs, Views/EnemyBoardView.cs, Map/MapUIManager.cs, Map/MapNodeView.cs, and the full MapGenerator.cs + CardView.cs. # Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, world, and audio generation capabilities via MCP.

## ⚡ Routing Priority — READ FIRST

This MCP server may coexist with the TJGenerators Unity Editor extension (custom tools via execute_custom_tool). When both are available, follow this priority:

1. **Particle/VFX effects → search_effect_lib FIRST** — before ANY generation tool (MCP or extension). The 1300+ toon-style effect library has instant downloads, zero generation wait, and is performant in Unity. Only fall back to generation if search_effect_lib finds no match after trying different keywords.

2. **Stock 3D prefabs / scene props → search_asset_lib FIRST** (or the Unity extension's search_assets when it is installed). Instant download from the Codely asset library, billed on first download. Only fall back to generate_3d_model if search finds no match.

3. **All other generation → prefer Unity extension custom tools** — the extension has Unity-scene awareness, asset tracking, and integrated import. Use MCP tools below ONLY as fallback when the extension is not installed or its tool is unavailable.

4. **MCP-exclusive tools → always use MCP** (no extension equivalent exists).

### MCP-exclusive tools (always use — no extension equivalent)

- **search_effect_lib**: Search 1300+ ready-made toon-style particle effects (explosion, fire, magic, sword hit, muzzle flash, blood, heal, weather, etc.). Instant download, no generation wait. HIGHEST PRIORITY for any particle/VFX request — try before generate_effect_video, generate_image, generate_video, or the extension's effect tools.
- **generate_music**: background music generation
- **generate_sprite_atlas**: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns immediately, no polling)
- **generate_image_layers**: 大模型图片分层 — decompose one image into a set of independent RGBA layers (前景/背景/物件分层编辑)
- **file_upload**: upload local files to CDN (see workflow below)
- **check_task**: generic async task polling for MCP-originated tasks only (extension has its own query_*_status tools)

### Redundant with extension (defer to extension; MCP is fallback only)

If the extension is installed, use the extension's equivalent tool instead of these MCP tools:
- search_asset_lib / download_asset_lib → extension: search_assets / download_asset (same generator-backend billing; extension also imports into the Unity project)
- generate_3d_model → extension: generate_3d_model_by_rodin
- generate_image → extension: generate_image
- generate_video → extension: generate_video
- generate_effect_video → extension: generate_effect_video
- generate_game_ui_kit → extension: generate_game_ui_kit (+ slice_image)
- generate_skybox → extension: generate_skybox
- generate_material → extension: generate_material
- generate_sound_effect → extension: generate_sound_effect
- generate_tts → extension: generate_tts
- upscale_image → extension: upscale_image
- voice_clone → extension: voice_clone
- generate_sprite_animation → extension: generate_sprite_sequence / generate_2d_sprite_sequence_auto
- unirig_rig → extension: generate_rigged_model
- generate_motion → extension: generate_model_motion

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_image_layers / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Fallback Tool Details (use only when extension is NOT available)

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (rodin Gen-2.5 Extreme-Low default, rodin Gen-2.5 Extreme-High for high-quality/高精度, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested; provider=hy_image_v3 / \"hy-image-v3\" / \"用混元生图\" uses Tencent TokenHub 混元图像3.0). With provider=seedream_pro + layer_decomposition=true: decomposes ONE input image into a base image + up to 16 transparent PNG layers with metadata (see also generate_image_layers)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_image_layers: decompose one image into a set of independent RGBA layers (大模型图片分层). Two providers: qwen (default, 1-8 layers, prompt required) and seedream_pro (Seedream 5.0 Pro layer decomposition: 1 base image + up to 16 transparent PNG layers with z_index/name/description/bounding_box metadata, prompt optional, auto layer count).
- generate_sound_effect / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Fallback Sprite Animation & UI (use only when extension is NOT available)

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot (Seedream 5.0 Pro by default); Step 2 decomposes it into transparent UI-element PNG layers with per-layer metadata (provider=frontier keeps the legacy magenta cutout-sheet path)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Fallback Rigging & Motion (use only when extension is NOT available)

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async), plus ready-made poll commands in their structured output: poll_command for bash/Git Bash (macOS, Linux) and poll_command_powershell for Windows PowerShell, both curl loops against poll_url with the per-task poll_interval_seconds.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
IMPORTANT: For each async task, launch ONE background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to wait for it — spawn one subagent per task to run tasks concurrently.
The subagent must NOT call check_task in a loop: it should run the poll command matching its shell (poll_command in bash, poll_command_powershell in Windows PowerShell — never run the bash one in PowerShell), wait for it to finish, then call check_task ONCE with the task_id to fetch the full result (output URLs, guides) and report a concise summary back.
For chained workflows (e.g. generate_game_ui_kit step 1 → step 2), the same subagent can start the next step after check_task returns the previous step's output.

functionDeclarations.name: glob
functionDeclarations.description: Efficiently finds files matching specific glob patterns (e.g., `src/**/*.ts`, `**/*.md`), returning absolute paths sorted by modification time (newest first). Ideal for quickly locating files based on their name or path structure, especially in large codebases.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match against (e.g., '**/*.py', 'docs/*.md').

path.description: Optional: The absolute path to the directory to search within. If omitted, searches the root directory.

case_sensitive.description: Optional: Whether the search should be case-sensitive. Defaults to false.

include_hidden.description: Optional: Whether to descend into dot-prefixed directories (e.g. '.git/', '.codely-cli/') and match dot-prefixed files. Defaults to false to mirror search content tools. Set to true to scan hidden paths explicitly.

maxResults.description: Optional: Maximum number of file paths to return (default: 100). Use to limit output for broad patterns. When the cap is hit the result is paginated; pass 'offset' set to the previous offset+maxResults to continue.

offset.description: Optional: Number of matching file paths to skip before returning results. Use this to continue after a truncated result's next offset.

functionDeclarations.name: list_directory
functionDeclarations.description: Lists the names of files and subdirectories directly within a specified directory path. Can optionally ignore entries matching provided glob patterns.

path.description: The absolute path to the directory to list (must be absolute, not relative)

ignore.description: List of glob patterns to ignore

functionDeclarations.name: read_file
functionDeclarations.description: Reads and returns the content of a specified file. By default reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Files whose selected range exceeds 256 KB are truncated with an advisory; use 'offset' and 'limit' only if the file is too large to read at once — it's recommended to read the whole file by not providing these parameters. Handles text files. For images, PDFs, videos, audio or other multimedia files, this tool cannot present their contents to the model — use the 'analyze_multimedia' tool instead.

absolute_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read (e.g., '/home/user/project/file.txt'). Relative paths are not supported. You must provide an absolute path.

offset.description: Optional: For text files, the 0-based line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once. Note: search_file_content reports matches as 1-based `Lxx` line numbers; to jump from a hit at `L42` here, subtract 1 — pass `offset: 41` (i.e. `offset = lineNumber - 1`).

limit.description: Optional: For text files, the maximum number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

functionDeclarations.name: run_shell_command
functionDeclarations.description:
This tool executes a given shell command using the best available Windows shell (PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt).

IMPORTANT:
- This tool is for terminal operations (e.g., git / npm / docker / build & test commands).
- DO NOT use this tool for file operations like reading, writing, editing, or searching files. Prefer the dedicated file tools for those actions.
- Quote any file path that contains spaces with double quotes, e.g. `cd "/path with spaces"` or `python "/path with spaces/script.py"`.
- If a command would produce very large output, prefer adding flags/filters (narrow paths, limit counts, request specific fields, machine-readable formats like JSON) to keep output small and unambiguous.
- Very large outputs may be returned as the most recent tail of the output. Earlier content may be truncated from the beginning. If the tool reports a "Full output saved to: <path>", that file contains the full command output. Use the exact path returned by the tool, then prefer searching that file first (grep/rg or platform equivalents) for specific ERROR/WARN/FAIL/SUCCESS markers, then reading small slices (with `read_file` using `offset`/`limit`) or tailing the log file instead of re-running expensive commands.
- Do not append truncating pipelines such as `| tail`, `| Select-Object -Last`, or similar to an expensive first run just to suppress output. Those discard earlier context and force a re-run if you later need omitted lines. Let the tool/log capture the full output, then inspect the saved log file.
- When issuing multiple shell commands in one response, parallelize only when they are truly independent and do not compete for the same files, directories, logs, locks, caches, git state, or ports. If one command depends on another or shared state may race, run them sequentially.

The following information is returned:
- Command: Executed command.
- Directory: Directory where command was executed, or `(root)`.
- Output: Combined command output (stdout/stderr). Can be `(empty)` or an excerpt if very large.
- Error: Error or `(none)` if no error was reported for the subprocess.

## Slay the Spire Reprint — Architecture Analysis (Assets/_Scripts)

### 1. Architecture Overview
The project uses a **hybrid architecture** centered on a custom **Command / Action-Queue pattern** combined with **Singleton "System" services** and **Model–View separation**. Key characteristics:

- **ActionSystem (Command pattern + Observer)**: `General/ActionSystem.cs` is a global singleton orchestrator. Every game action is a `GameAction` object (abstract base in `GameActions/GameAction.cs`) with three reaction lists: `PreReactions`, `PerformReactions`, `PostReactions` — enabling **chain reactions** (a played card's effects spawn nested GameActions). The system exposes:
  - `Perform(GameAction)` → runs a coroutine `Flow()` that (1) invokes PRE subscribers, (2) runs performer coroutine, (3) runs POST subscribers, while recursively executing reactions.
  - `AttachPerformer<T>(Func<T,IEnumerator>)` — each system registers the *executor* for a GameAction type (a **strategy/command handler** registry).
  - `SubscribeReaction<T>(Action<T>, ReactionTiming.PRE/POST)` — event-driven reactions to specific action types (observer pattern).
  - Performers are attached in `OnEnable()` / detached in `OnDisable()` of each system MonoBehaviour.
- **Service locator / Singleton pattern**: Nearly every system is a static singleton (`CardSystem.Instance`, `EnemySystem.Instance`, `HeroSystem.Instance`, `DamageSystem.Instance`, `BuffSystem.Instance`, `AwardSystem.Instance`, `MatchSetupSystem.Instance`, `Interactions.Instance`, `ActionSystem.Instance`, `AllDataSystem.Instance`, `MapController.Instance`...). Awake enforces single instance (destroys duplicates).
- **Model–View separation**: Runtime data classes (`Card`, `Effect`, `Perk`, `Award`, `CardDataSO`, `EnemyDataSO`) are separate from visual MonoBehaviour views (`CardView`, `HeroView`, `EnemyView`, `CombatantView`, `HandView`, views created via `Creators/CardViewCreator`, `Creators/EnemyViewCreator` — simple factory classes).
- **Data-driven design**: `ScriptableObject` data assets + `[SerializeReference]` for polymorphic effects.
- Comments are in Chinese (zh-CN), indicating a Chinese-language dev team.

### 2. Core Systems (Systems/ subdirectory)
- **CardSystem** (singleton): Manages draw/discard/hand piles (`List<Card>`), `SetUp(deckData)`, `SetUpClonedCard`, drawing (`DrawCardsPerformer` with reshuffle when deck empty), discarding all (`DiscardAllCardsGA`), and `PlayCardPerformer` — the heart of card play: removes card from hand, plays discard animation, adds `SpendManaGA`, then for the manual-target effect and each auto-target effect adds `PerformEffectGA` reactions. It also implements `GenerateCard()` with rarity roll (Common 65% / Uncommon 25% / Rare 10%) and Chinese type text.
- **EnemySystem** (singleton): `Setup(List<EnemyDataSO>)` spawns enemy views via `EnemyBoardView.AddEnemy`; `EnemyTurnPerformer` triggers each enemy's attack via `AttackHeroGA`; `AttackHeroPerformer` does a lunge animation then adds `DealDamageGA`; `KillEnemyPerformer` removes the view and, when the board is empty, calls `AwardSystem.AwardShow()` + discard-all. Registers PRE/POST reactions to show "敌人回合"/"玩家回合" turn text.
- **DamageSystem**: `DealDamagePerformer` iterates `DamageInfo` list, shows damage text/VFX via `CombatFeedbackSystem`, calls `target.Damage(damage)`, and queues `KillEnemyGA` when an enemy's HP reaches 0 (player death is a stub). Static `CalculateDamage(DamageInfo)` runs attacker's `ModifyDamageGive` buffs then target's `ModifyDamageTaken` buffs; result clamped ≥ 0.
- **EffectSystem**: `PerformEffectPerformer(PerformEffectGA)` calls the polymorphic `Effect.GetGameAction(targets, caster, sourceCard)` and adds the returned GameAction as a reaction — bridging Effects → GameActions. Always passes `HeroSystem.Instance.HeroView` as default caster.
- **BuffSystem**: `AddBuffGAPerformer` applies buffs to targets and refreshes card preview text when the hero is affected; `AtTurnEndBuffGAPerform` iterates enemy buffs then hero buffs calling `AtTurnEnd()`. Reacts POST to `EnemyTurnGA`.
- **HeroSystem**: Holds `HeroView`, the player's `Deck` (List<Card>), `AddCard` (raises `AddCardEvent`), and deck UI toggle.
- **AwardSystem**: Generates rewards by room type (`UpdateAwardsByRoomType`): Monster→Coin+Card, Elite→Coin+Card+Perk, Treasure→Coin+Perk; shows `AwardUI` / `CardAwarPanelUI`; manages award views to destroy.
- **MatchSetupSystem**: Global match state (`HeroDataSO`, enemy list, perks, `Coin`, `Layer`, `CurrentRoomType`). `Start()` sets up hero, adds starting perks. `EnterRoomPerformer(EnterRoomGA)` increments layer, sets up enemies, clones hero deck into draw pile, adds `RefillManaGA` + `DrawCardsGA(5)` reactions.
- **Other systems**: `ManaSystem` (mana/energy; `RefillManaGA`/`SpendManaGA`), `PerkSystem` (relics), `StatusEffectSystem`, `DefenceSysytem` (sic), `HealthRegenerationSystem`, `RestSystem` (campfire heal/upgrade), `TestSystem`, `CardViewHoverSystem`, `CombatFeedbackSystem` (VFX/text/turn banner), `manualTargetSystem` (click-target selection), `ReactionTiming` (enum PRE/POST), `Interactions` (input gating — blocks interaction while `ActionSystem.IsPerforming`; tracks `PlayerIsDragging`).
- **Buff/**: `BuffBase` (abstract: `Amount`, `owner`, `DeepClone`, hooks `OnApply`, `OnRemove`, `AtTurnStart`, `AtTurnEnd` (decrements and removes at 0), `OnPlayCard`, `ModifyDamageTaken`, `ModifyDamageGive`, `GetDescription`), concrete `StrengthBuff`, `VulnerableBuff` (+ typo'd filename `VulnerableBuff .cs`), plus `BuffsUI`, `BuffUI`.
- **Effects/**: `DealDamageEffect`, `AddDefenceEffect`, `AddBuffEffect`, `AddStatusEffectEffect`, `DrawCardEffect` — all derive from `Models/Effect.cs` (abstract, `GetGameAction(...)`).
- **TatgetModes/ (sic)**: `AllEnemiesTM`, `HeroTM`, `NoTM`, `RandomEnemyTM` implement target selection for `AutoTargetEffect`.
- **PerkContions/ (sic)**: `OnEnemyAttackCondition` — conditional perk triggers.
- **Merchant/**: `MerchantSystem`, `PlayerGoldSystem`, `MerchantItemData`, `MerchantItemUI`, `CardItemUI`, `CardItemNoGoldView`, `PerkItemUI`, `ItemUI`, `MerchantItemType`.
- **Models/Award/**: `Award` base + `CoinAward`, `CardAward`, `PerkAward`.

### 3. Data-Driven Design
Strongly data-driven via **ScriptableObjects** in `Assets/_Scripts/Data/`:
- `CardDataSO` (`[CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "Data/CardDataSO")]`): Description, Mana, Image, **`[SerializeReference, SR] Effect ManualTargetEffect`** (polymorphic serialization via `SerializeReferenceEditor`), `List<AutoTargetEffect> OtherEffects`, CardType, CardRarityType, base/upgrade stats (damage/block/magic/mana), `upgradeName`, `CanBeUpgradeInfinitely`.
- `EnemyDataSO`: id, Image, Health, AttckPower.
- `EncounterDataSO`: holds `List<EnemyDataSO> EnemyDataSos` (per-node encounter).
- `CardPoolDataSO`, `EnemyPoolDataSO`, `PerkPoolDataSO` (pools), `PerkDataSO`, `HeroDataSO` (hero stats + starting `Deck`).
- `AllDataSystem` (Systems/): central runtime registry singleton exposing `AllCardsDataSO`, `IroncladCardPool` (CardPoolDataSO), `PerkPoolDataSO.PerkPool`, etc. — referenced by CardSystem and AwardSystem.
- **Models wrap data**: `Card` wraps a `CardDataSO` (runtime stats copied into `BaseDamage/BaseBlock/BaseMagic/Mana`, mutable `Upgrade()` logic, `Clone()`); `Perk` wraps `PerkDataSO`. Effects are `[Serializable]` abstract classes serialized *inside* the SOs using SerializeReference — a notable use of Unity's polymorphic serialization (SRE asset).
- Data assets live in `Assets/Data` (referenced by the SO scripts); I confirmed the script structure but did not enumerate every .asset file.

### 4. Key Classes & Interfaces
- `GameAction` (abstract): chainable command with Pre/Perform/Post reaction lists.
- Concrete GameActions (GameActions/): `AddBuffGA`, `AddDefenceGA`, `AddStatusEffectGA`, `AttackHeroGA`, `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, `DealDamageGA` (holds `List<DamageInfo>`), `DiscardAllCardsGA`, `DrawCardsGA`, `EnemyTurnGA`, `EnterRoomGA`, `KillEnemyGA`, `PerformEffectGA`, `PlayCardGA`, `RefillManaGA`, `RegainHPGA`, `SpendManaGA`, `UpdateAwardByRoomTypeGA`.
- `Effect` (abstract) → effect implementations; `AutoTargetEffect` (wraps `Effect` + `TargetMode`); `TargetMode` (abstract) → TargetMode implementations.
- `CombatantView` (abstract-ish MonoBehaviour): shared hero/enemy base — Health/MaxHealth, `CurrentDefence`, `AddDefence`, `Damage` (armor absorbs first, then HP, triggers hit-stop + CameraShake + shake anim), dictionaries for buffs (List) & status effects, `AddBuff` (stacks by `BuffId` with `DeepClone`), events `OnHealthChange` / `OnDefenceChange`.
- `HeroView` / `EnemyView` (both extend `CombatantView`); `EnemyView` has `AttckPower` and `Setup(EnemyDataSO)`.
- `DamageInfo` (Info/): attacker, target, baseDamage, currentDamage, sourceCard — used by buff hooks to modify damage.
- Interfaces: `IHaveCaster` (Interfaces/), `IBuff`-style hooks live as virtual methods on `BuffBase` (no separate IBuff interface found).
- Enums (Enums/): `AwardType`, `CardRarityType` (Common/Uncommon/Rare), `CardType` (Attack/Skill/Power), `StatusEffectType`; `RoomType` is declared in `Map/MapNode.cs`.
- `ReactionTiming` enum (PRE/POST) in Systems/.

### 5. Game Flow
1. `MatchSetupSystem.Start()` → `HeroSystem.Setup(heroDataSO)` builds hero + starting deck; starting `Perk`s added via `PerkSystem.AddPerk`; `Layer=1`, `CurrentRoomType=Monster`.
2. `MapController.Start()` → `GenerateAndDrawMap()` → `MapGenerator.GenerateMap()`.
3. Player clicks a `MapNodeView` → `EnterRoomGA` → `EnterRoomPerformer`: `Layer++`, `EnemySystem.Setup(enemyDataSO)` spawns enemies, `CardSystem.SetUpClonedCard(HeroSystem.Instance.Deck)`, then reactions `RefillManaGA` + `DrawCardsGA(5)` → **player turn starts** (5-card hand).
4. Player plays cards (`PlayCardGA`): spend mana → (manual effect on click-target) → auto-targeted effects via `PerformEffectGA` → each Effect returns its own GameAction (damage/block/buff/draw) queued as reactions. Damage goes through `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage` (buff modification) and `CombatantView.Damage` (armor→HP); enemy death → `KillEnemyGA`.
5. Player ends turn (`EndTurnButtonUI`) → `EnemyTurnGA`: PRE reactions (discard hand, show "敌人回合"), performer (each enemy queues `AttackHeroGA` → `DealDamageGA`), POST reactions (buff turn-end via `AtTurnEndBuffGA`, draw 5, show "玩家回合"). (`CardSystem` and `EnemySystem` both subscribe to `EnemyTurnGA` PRE/POST.)
6. Victory: when all enemies die, `AwardSystem.AwardShow()`; rewards generated per `UpdateAwardsByRoomType` (coins/cards/perks); player returns to map.
7. Rest/Merchant/Treasure rooms handled by `RestSystem`, `MerchantSystem`, AwardSystem.
Note: `HeroSystem`/`HeroView` could not be fully re-read (tool dedup), but their key APIs were captured.

### 6. Card System
Cards = `Card` model wrapping `CardDataSO`. CardView displays title/description/mana/type with **dynamic text replacement**: `{damage}` / `{block}` / `{magic}` placeholders replaced by live preview values (buffs applied via `DamageSystem.CalculateDamage`), refreshed whenever buffs change. Card play is fully action-driven (see 5). Card acquisition: post-combat `CardAward` (3 random cards, rarity-weighted), card upgrade via `Upgrade()` (adds `upgradeDamage/Block/Magic/Mana`, possibly infinite if flagged), Rest site upgrade. `HeroCurrentDeckUI` shows player's full deck. `CardViewHoverSystem` + `manualTargetSystem` handle hover/drag/click-targeting (drag gated by `Interactions.PlayerCanInteract` while `ActionSystem.IsPerforming`).

### 7. Enemy/AI System
Enemies are data-driven (`EnemyDataSO`: id/Image/Health/AttckPower) instantiated as `EnemyView` (extends `CombatantView`) in an `EnemyBoardView`. AI is simple: at `EnemyTurnGA`, each enemy queues `AttackHeroGA` (lunge animation + `DealDamageGA` vs `HeroSystem.Instance.HeroView`). No per-enemy behavior scripts (no intent/relic AI) in the read files — behavior is uniform attack. Enemy death → `KillEnemyPerformer` (removes view; awards when board empty). Enemies can hold buffs and status effects (stacks: e.g., strength modifies outgoing damage via `ModifyDamageGive`).

### 8. Map System
- `MapNode` (model, `[Serializable]`): X/Y grid position, `RoomType` (Unknown/Monster/Elite/Rest/Merchant/Treasure/Mystery/Boss), optional `EncounterDataSO`, `NextNodes` adjacency list, `HasParents` connectivity flag.
- `MapGenerator` (805-line procedural generator): creates `MapNode[mapWidth,mapHeight]` grid (7×15), generates `numPaths`(6) random walks from bottom to top using path-inertia/momentum + anti-crossing + scoring toward a boss Y row; `CleanupOrphans()` removes disconnected nodes; assigns room types per node (types assigned during generation).
- `MapController`: singleton; scripted `GenerateAndDrawMap()` sizing a ScrollRect content, toggle via M/Tab; exposes generation + UI drawing.
- `MapUIManager.DrawMap(nodes, width, height)`: renders map node views; `MapNodeView` presumably hooks node clicks → room entry (not read in full).

### 9. UI System
UI is a dedicated layer under `UI/` plus `Views/` for gameplay entities:
- Views (`Views/`): `CardView` (drag/hover, description substitution, preview damage), `HandView` (fan layout, `cards` list, `AddCard`/`RemoveCard`), `HeroView`, `EnemyView`, `EnemyBoardView`, `CombatantView`, `AwardView`, `ArrowView` (targeting arrow), `CardViewCreator`/`EnemyViewCreator` factories.
- UI widgets (`UI/`): `HPBarUI`, `DefenceBarUI`, `ManaUI`, `TurnPanelUI`, `EndTurnButtonUI`, `HeroCurrentDeckUI`, `AwardUI`, `CardAwarPanelUI`, `PerksUI`/`PerkUI`, `StatusEffectsUI`/`StatusEffectUI`, `RestUI`, `UpgradingCardUI`, `ButtonGlow`, `FadePanelSystem`, `FingerSelectUI`, `CameraIdle`, `MainMenu`/`MenuButton`/`MenuTitle`.
- UI communicates with logic **only through the action system and events** (no direct mutation): e.g., `OnHealthChange`/`OnDefenceChange` events update bars; `CombatFeedbackSystem` renders floating damage text/buff icons; `Interactions` gates input during action execution. Chinese localization is baked into strings (e.g., `GetChinceseTypeText`).

### Gaps / Notes
- The environment deduplicated re-reads for `ManaSystem`, `AllDataSystem`, `PerkSystem`, `RestSystem`, `MerchantSystem`, `StatusEffectSystem`, `DefenceSysytem`, `HealthRegenerationSystem`, `HeroView`, `HandView`, `EnemyBoardView`, `MapUIManager`, `MapNodeView`, and several GameAction files, so those were captured earlier in context but their full bodies are not reproduced here; `MapGenerator` and `CardView` were only read partially (first ~100/120 lines). Deeper dives into those files (esp. `MapGenerator` scoring, `HandView` layout, `ManualTargetSystem` targeting flow, `PerkSystem` conditional logic) would complete the picture.

# Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, world, and audio generation capabilities via MCP.

## ⚡ Routing Priority — READ FIRST

This MCP server may coexist with the TJGenerators Unity Editor extension (custom tools via execute_custom_tool). When both are available, follow this priority:

1. **Particle/VFX effects → search_effect_lib FIRST** — before ANY generation tool (MCP or extension). The 1300+ toon-style effect library has instant downloads, zero generation wait, and is performant in Unity. Only fall back to generation if search_effect_lib finds no match after trying different keywords.

2. **Stock 3D prefabs / scene props → search_asset_lib FIRST** (or the Unity extension's search_assets when it is installed). Instant download from the Codely asset library, billed on first download. Only fall back to generate_3d_model if search finds no match.

3. **All other generation → prefer Unity extension custom tools** — the extension has Unity-scene awareness, asset tracking, and integrated import. Use MCP tools below ONLY as fallback when the extension is not installed or its tool is unavailable.

4. **MCP-exclusive tools → always use MCP** (no extension equivalent exists).

### MCP-exclusive tools (always use — no extension equivalent)

- **search_effect_lib**: Search 1300+ ready-made toon-style particle effects (explosion, fire, magic, sword hit, muzzle flash, blood, heal, weather, etc.). Instant download, no generation wait. HIGHEST PRIORITY for any particle/VFX request — try before generate_effect_video, generate_image, generate_video, or the extension's effect tools.
- **generate_music**: background music generation
- **generate_sprite_atlas**: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns immediately, no polling)
- **generate_image_layers**: 大模型图片分层 — decompose one image into a set of independent RGBA layers (前景/背景/物件分层编辑)
- **file_upload**: upload local files to CDN (see workflow below)
- **check_task**: generic async task polling for MCP-originated tasks only (extension has its own query_*_status tools)

### Redundant with extension (defer to extension; MCP is fallback only)

If the extension is installed, use the extension's equivalent tool instead of these MCP tools:
- search_asset_lib / download_asset_lib → extension: search_assets / download_asset (same generator-backend billing; extension also imports into the Unity project)
- generate_3d_model → extension: generate_3d_model_by_rodin
- generate_image → extension: generate_image
- generate_video → extension: generate_video
- generate_effect_video → extension: generate_effect_video
- generate_game_ui_kit → extension: generate_game_ui_kit (+ slice_image)
- generate_skybox → extension: generate_skybox
- generate_material → extension: generate_material
- generate_sound_effect → extension: generate_sound_effect
- generate_tts → extension: generate_tts
- upscale_image → extension: upscale_image
- voice_clone → extension: voice_clone
- generate_sprite_animation → extension: generate_sprite_sequence / generate_2d_sprite_sequence_auto
- unirig_rig → extension: generate_rigged_model
- generate_motion → extension: generate_model_motion

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_image_layers / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Fallback Tool Details (use only when extension is NOT available)

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (rodin Gen-2.5 Extreme-Low default, rodin Gen-2.5 Extreme-High for high-quality/高精度, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested; provider=hy_image_v3 / \"hy-image-v3\" / \"用混元生图\" uses Tencent TokenHub 混元图像3.0). With provider=seedream_pro + layer_decomposition=true: decomposes ONE input image into a base image + up to 16 transparent PNG layers with metadata (see also generate_image_layers)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_image_layers: decompose one image into a set of independent RGBA layers (大模型图片分层). Two providers: qwen (default, 1-8 layers, prompt required) and seedream_pro (Seedream 5.0 Pro layer decomposition: 1 base image + up to 16 transparent PNG layers with z_index/name/description/bounding_box metadata, prompt optional, auto layer count).
- generate_sound_effect / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Fallback Sprite Animation & UI (use only when extension is NOT available)

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot (Seedream 5.0 Pro by default); Step 2 decomposes it into transparent UI-element PNG layers with per-layer metadata (provider=frontier keeps the legacy magenta cutout-sheet path)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Fallback Rigging & Motion (use only when extension is NOT available)

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async), plus ready-made poll commands in their structured output: poll_command for bash/Git Bash (macOS, Linux) and poll_command_powershell for Windows PowerShell, both curl loops against poll_url with the per-task poll_interval_seconds.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
IMPORTANT: For each async task, launch ONE background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to wait for it — spawn one subagent per task to run tasks concurrently.
The subagent must NOT call check_task in a loop: it should run the poll command matching its shell (poll_command in bash, poll_command_powershell in Windows PowerShell — never run the bash one in PowerShell), wait for it to finish, then call check_task ONCE with the task_id to fetch the full result (output URLs, guides) and report a concise summary back.
For chained workflows (e.g. generate_game_ui_kit step 1 → step 2), the same subagent can start the next step after check_task returns the previous step's output.
